issues.legal_issue: A defective appeal filed before a statutory bar on that class of appeals takes effect remains pending from its original filing when the court permits the court-fee deficiency to be cured and the deficiency is later made good.
material_facts: A special appeal from a single judge’s judgment in appellate jurisdiction was presented before the law abolishing that class of appeals took effect.
The memorandum was deficient in court-fee when presented. The court allowed the deficiency to be made good, and the appellant paid it after the abolition law had taken effect.
The memorandum was not rejected; after the deficiency was paid, it was accepted and registered.
The abolition law barred the relevant class of appeals but preserved appeals that were pending immediately before the law took effect.
issues.conclusion: The appeal was pending from the date it was originally presented and was preserved by the exception for pending appeals. The statutory bar did not apply, and the appeal was to be heard.
issues.legal_principle: Under Order 41, rule 1 of the Code of Civil Procedure, an appeal is instituted by presenting a memorandum of appeal. Section 149 of the Code permits the court, in its discretion, to allow a deficient court-fee to be paid later; upon payment, the document has the same force and effect as if the fee had been paid initially. Section 149 must be read harmoniously with section 4 of the Court Fees Act, as a proviso permitting the deficiency to be cured, so the appeal is treated as pending from its original presentation. This applies the pending-appeal exception in section 3(2) of the U.P. High Court (Abolition of Letters Patent Appeals) Act, 1962, notwithstanding its general bar in section 3(1). The reasoning is supported by Gavarnga Sahu v. Botokrishna Patro, Faizullah v. Mauladad, Wajid Ali v. Isar Bano, and Nagendra Nath v. Suresh.

rule.if: special_appeal_covered_by_new_bar and memorandum_presented_before_bar_took_effect and court_fee_deficient_at_presentation and court_allowed_time_to_cure and fee_deficiency_later_cured and appeal_not_rejected

predicates.special_appeal_covered_by_new_bar: The proceeding was a special appeal of a kind that a newly effective legal bar would otherwise prohibit.
predicates.memorandum_presented_before_bar_took_eff: The appellant presented the appeal memorandum before the new bar took effect.
predicates.court_fee_deficient_at_presentation: The fee paid with the memorandum was less than the required fee when it was presented.
predicates.court_allowed_time_to_cure: The court allowed the appellant time to make good the fee deficiency.
predicates.fee_deficiency_later_cured: The appellant later paid the deficiency as permitted by the court.
predicates.appeal_not_rejected: The court did not reject the appeal memorandum before the deficiency was cured.

issues.definition: When a special appeal within a newly barred category is presented before the bar takes effect with a fee deficiency that the court allows and the appellant cures without the appeal being rejected, the appeal counts as pending from its original presentation and is saved from the bar.
